tool.name: minibwa
tool.description: - map short and accurate long reads against a reference genome
tool.command:
@pipefail@ @set_reference_index@
## Begin minibwa command line
minibwa map -t "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}"
## Library type. --hic is equivalent to -5P, --meth requires an index built with --meth. #if str( $mode ) == "hic": --hic #elif str( $mode ) == "meth": --meth #end if
#if str( $output_format.output_format_selector ) == "paf": -f ${output_format.chain_only} #end if
#if str( $analysis_type.analysis_type_selector ) == "full": ## Mapping options #if str( $analysis_type.mapping_options.mapping_options_selector ) == "set": -x '${analysis_type.mapping_options.x}' -k '${analysis_type.mapping_options.k}' -c '${analysis_type.mapping_options.c}' -g '${analysis_type.mapping_options.g}' -w '${analysis_type.mapping_options.w}' -W '${analysis_type.mapping_options.W}' -m '${analysis_type.mapping_options.m}' -p '${analysis_type.mapping_options.p}' -N '${analysis_type.mapping_options.N}' -l '${analysis_type.mapping_options.l}' #end if
## Alignment (scoring) options #if str( $analysis_type.alignment_options.alignment_options_selector ) == "set": -A '${analysis_type.alignment_options.A}' -B '${analysis_type.alignment_options.B}' -O '${analysis_type.alignment_options.O}' -E '${analysis_type.alignment_options.E}' -s '${analysis_type.alignment_options.s}' #end if
## Paired-end options #if str( $analysis_type.paired_options.paired_options_selector ) == "set": ${analysis_type.paired_options.P} --rescue='${analysis_type.paired_options.rescue}' #end if
## Input/output options #if str( $analysis_type.io_options.io_options_selector ) == "set": ${analysis_type.io_options.u} ${analysis_type.io_options.y} ${analysis_type.io_options.Y} ${analysis_type.io_options.five} --outn='${analysis_type.io_options.outn}' --outs='${analysis_type.io_options.outs}' --xa='${analysis_type.io_options.xa}' #if str( $analysis_type.io_options.b ) != "none": -b '${analysis_type.io_options.b}' #end if #if str( $analysis_type.io_options.K ): -K '${analysis_type.io_options.K}' #end if #if $analysis_type.io_options.H: -H '${analysis_type.io_options.H}' #end if #if str( $analysis_type.io_options.mmap ) != "none": '${analysis_type.io_options.mmap}' #end if #end if #end if
## Handle read group options... #if str( $rg.rg_selector ) == "set": @set_rg_string@ -R '$rg_string' #end if
#if str( $fastq_input.fastq_input_selector ) == "paired_collection": ## check that insert statistics is used #if str( $fastq_input.iset_stats ): -I '${fastq_input.iset_stats}' #end if
'${reference_index}' '${fastq_input.fastq_input1.forward}' '${fastq_input.fastq_input1.reverse}' #else: '${reference_index}' '${fastq_input.fastq_input1}' #end if
## Convert the SAM output to BAM. ## The stages of a pipe run in parallel, so no stage that runs while minibwa is ## still mapping may claim \$GALAXY_SLOTS as well, as that would overcommit the ## cores allocated to the job. Using the two pipe stages has the following effect ## - minibwa and sort run in parallel, during this time sort is single threaded ## and writes uncompressed temporary files, but produces no output (hence ## view does not run) ## - once minibwa is finished sort merges the temporary files (which should be ## fast also on a single thread) and gives the sorted output to view, which ## only compresses it (now using full parallelism again) #if str( $output_format.output_format_selector ) == "paf": > '$paf_output' #elif str( $output_format.output_sort ) == "coordinate": | samtools sort --no-PG -l 0 -T "\${TMPDIR:-.}" -O bam | samtools view --no-PG -O bam -@ "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" -o '$bam_output' #elif str( $output_format.output_sort ) == "name": | samtools sort -n --no-PG -l 0 -T "\${TMPDIR:-.}" -O bam | samtools view --no-PG -O bam -@ "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" -o '$bam_output' #else ## Nothing buffers the stream here, so this stage runs alongside minibwa the ## whole time and is deliberately left single threaded. | samtools view --no-PG -O bam -o '$bam_output' #end if

param.label: Single or Paired-end reads
param.help: Select between paired and single end data

param.name: fastq_input1
param.label: Select fastq dataset
param.help: Specify dataset with single reads

param.label: Select a paired collection
param.help: See help section for an explanation of dataset collections

param.name: iset_stats
param.label: Enter mean, standard deviation, max, and min for insert lengths.
param.help: -I; This parameter is only used for paired reads. Only mean is required while sd, max, and min will be inferred. Examples: both "250" and "250,25" will work while "250,,10" will not. See below for details.

param.name: mode
param.label: Library type
param.help: Bisulfite mapping needs an FM-index built with --meth. For a reference from your history this index is built automatically; a built-in index must have been created with the 'Build the additional BS-seq index' option of the minibwa index builder data manager.

param.label: Set mapping options?
param.help: Sets -x, -k, -c, -g, -w, -W, -m, -p, -N and -l options.

param.label: Preset
param.help: -x; default=adap. In the adaptive mode minibwa changes several internal parameters per read based on the read length, so mixed short and long reads can be mapped in one run.
param.option: adap - mixed short and long reads (adaptive)

param.label: Minimum seed length
param.help: -k; default=19

param.label: Skip seeds with more than that many occurrences
param.help: -c; default=250

param.label: Maximum gap size
param.help: -g; default=100; controls both extension and chain breaking

param.label: Bandwidth for banded alignment
param.help: -w; default=100

param.label: Long bandwidth
param.help: -W; default=20000; used for long reads and in the adaptive mode

param.label: Minimum chaining score
param.help: -m; default=25

param.label: Minimum secondary-to-primary score ratio
param.help: -p; default=0.5

param.label: Retain at most this many secondary alignments
param.help: -N; default=50; this is the number kept internally, see --outn for how many are written out

param.label: Treat reads shorter than this as short reads in the adaptive mode
param.help: -l; default=325; only effective with the adaptive preset

param.name: alignment_options_selector
param.label: Set alignment scoring options?
param.help: Sets -A, -B, -O, -E and -s options.

param.label: Score for a sequence match
param.help: -A; default=2

param.label: Penalty for a mismatch
param.help: -B; default=8

param.label: Gap open penalties
param.help: -O; default=12,23; a two-piece affine gap cost, given as INT1[,INT2]

param.label: Gap extension penalties
param.help: -E; default=2,1; a gap of size k costs min(O1 + k*E1, O2 + k*E2)

param.label: Minimum score to output
param.help: -s; default=30; suppress an alignment with a DP score lower than this value times the match score

param.label: Set paired-end options?
param.help: Sets -P and --rescue options. These only have an effect on paired input.

param.label: Skip pairing and mate rescue
param.help: -P; reads are mapped as if they were single-end

param.label: Perform mate rescue for up to this many candidates
param.help: --rescue; default=10; 0 skips mate rescue

param.name: io_options_selector
param.label: Set input/output options?
param.help: Sets -u, -y, -Y, -5, --outn, --outs, --xa, -b and -K options.

param.label: Copy FASTA/Q comments to the output
Use soft clipping for supplementary alignments
param.help: -Y; by default supplementary alignments are hard clipped

param.name: five
param.label: For split alignment, take the alignment with the smallest query coordinate as primary
param.help: -5; useful for Hi-C data. The Hi-C library type already implies this option.

param.label: Output up to this many secondary alignments
param.help: --outn; default=0; capped by the -N value

param.label: Output a secondary hit if its score is at least this fraction of the best score
param.help: --outs; default=0.8

param.label: Write up to this many hits to the XA tag
param.help: --xa; default=5; only hits scoring above 80% of the best hit are considered

param.label: Output a base alignment tag
param.help: -b; by default no base-level tag is written

param.label: Process this many bases of query sequence per batch
param.help: -K; default=100m,1g; given as NUM1[,NUM2], e.g. 100m or 100m,1g

param.label: Insert these lines into the SAM header
param.help: -H; a text file whose lines are inserted into the header, e.g. @CO comment lines

param.label: Load the index via memory mapped files
param.help: --mmap; reduces the resident memory of the job at the cost of slower mapping
param.option: No, load the index into memory
Yes, memory map the whole index
Yes, memory map only part of the index (lite)

param.name: output_sort
param.label: BAM sorting mode
param.option: Sort by read names (i.e., the QNAME field)

param.label: Perform chaining only, without base alignment
param.help: --chain-only; much faster, but the output contains no CIGAR. Only available for PAF output.

tool.help:
**What it does**
minibwa is a successor to BWA-MEM that aligns short reads and accurate long reads to a reference genome. It combines the variable-length seeding of BWA-MEM with the chaining and base-level alignment of minimap2, and is reported to be about four times as fast as BWA-MEM and more than twice as fast as BWA-MEM2 at comparable accuracy.
In its default *adaptive* mode minibwa changes several internal parameters per read based on the read length, so a mixture of short and accurate long reads can be mapped in a single run without manual tuning. Besides ordinary genomic reads it also handles Hi-C reads and *directional* bisulfite sequencing reads natively.
minibwa does **not** support spliced alignment, noisy long reads, undirectional bisulfite data, or alternate haplotype recognition.
The Galaxy implementation takes fastq (or fasta) files as input and produces output in BAM format, which can be further processed using the various BAM utilities in Galaxy (BAMTools, SAMTools, Picard), or in PAF format.
-----
**Indices: Selecting reference genomes for minibwa**
The wrapper lets you select between precomputed (built-in) and user-defined indices for reference genomes using the **Will you select a reference genome from your history or use a built-in index?** flag. This flag has two options:
1. **Use a built-in genome index** - Galaxy provides a **Using reference genome** dropdown, populated with genomes that were pre-indexed with the ``minibwa index`` utility and are ready to be mapped against. 2. **Use a reference from history and build index if necessary** - Galaxy provides a dropdown populated with FASTA files in your current history. Selecting one causes Galaxy to first transparently index it with ``minibwa index`` and then run ``minibwa map``.
Unlike minimap2, ``minibwa map`` cannot index a reference on the fly, so the index is always built as a separate step before mapping. For a reference from your history, the collapsed **Index building options** section exposes the options of ``minibwa index``: the random seed for ambiguous bases (``-s``), the suffix array sample rate (``-u``, a larger value gives a smaller index but slower mapping) and the low-memory BWT construction algorithm (``-l``, single threaded, with its block size ``-b``), which helps when a large genome does not index within the memory of the job. For built-in indexes these choices were made by the administrator when the index builder data manager was run.
-----
**Library type**
* *Genomic DNA* - the default mode. * *Hi-C reads* - passes ``--hic``, which is equivalent to ``-5P``: pairing and mate rescue are skipped and the alignment with the smallest query coordinate becomes the primary one. * *Directional bisulfite sequencing reads* - passes ``--meth``. This mode needs an additional FM-index built with ``minibwa index --meth``. When the reference comes from your history the wrapper builds it automatically. A **built-in** index only works in this mode if the administrator ticked *Build the additional BS-seq index* when running the minibwa index builder data manager; otherwise the job fails with a "failed to load the index" error.
-----
**Galaxy-specific option**
The **Select analysis mode** menu offers two levels of control:
1. *Simple mode*: aligns single or paired-end data to the reference using default parameters. Equivalent to ``minibwa map <reference index> <fastq dataset1> [fastq dataset2]``. 2. *Full list of options*: exposes the mapping, alignment scoring, paired-end and input/output options through the Galaxy interface. The input/output section also lets you insert extra lines into the SAM header from a text file (``-H``, e.g. ``@CO`` comment lines) and load the index through memory mapped files (``--mmap``), which lowers the resident memory of the job at the cost of slower mapping.
The only ``minibwa map`` options the wrapper does not expose are ``-t`` and ``-o``, which Galaxy sets itself, and ``-f``, which follows from the chosen output format. The legacy ``minibwa mem`` interface is not wrapped, since upstream does not recommend it.
-----
**Paired-end reads**
Paired reads are passed to minibwa as a paired dataset collection, which keeps the two mates associated with each other and lets the tool be mapped over many samples at once. minibwa has no smart-pairing option, so a single file with interleaved paired reads has to be de-interleaved first (for example with the *FASTQ de-interlacer* tool) and the two resulting datasets built into a paired collection before they can be mapped as a pair.
-----
**Output format**
* *BAM* - minibwa writes SAM, which the wrapper converts to BAM. The records can be sorted by chromosomal coordinate, by read name (the QNAME field), or left in input order. The order of the alignment records does not depend on the number of threads, so all three modes use all allocated cores. * *PAF* - the compact minimap2 pairwise mapping format. The **Perform chaining only** option is available here: it skips base-level alignment entirely, which is much faster but yields no CIGAR string. That option is not offered for BAM output because chain-only results cannot be converted to a valid BAM file.
